claim: Kalshi distributions for FOMC, CPI, core CPI, PCE, unemployment, payrolls, GDP, recession are well-behaved and respond sharply to news; variance of the fed funds distribution falls after data releases (2022-2025); Kalshi mode matched every FOMC decision on the day before since 2022 (significantly better than fed funds futures); headline CPI forecasts significantly better than the Bloomberg consensus; core CPI and unemployment similar to consensus. No asset-return test.
quote: for headline CPI, we find Kalshi provides a statistically significant improvement over the Bloomberg consensus forecast.
limitations: Text extracted from the PDF by the lead (not publisher HTML). Tests forecast accuracy and news response of the distributions, not equity returns; early Kalshi years are thin and tail strikes can be stale; a Kalshi series is not a consensus survey.
independent_replication: No independent replication of the forecasting claims found; the MIT fork WillBtK/macro_kalshi rebuilds the distribution construction from the same replication package.
impact_on_spec: Direct basis of the data and mechanism: Kalshi distributions are well-behaved, respond to news and their variance falls after releases, so the standard deviation of the distribution the afternoon before a release is a usable release-specific uncertainty measure. No asset-return result, which is what this iteration tests.

claim: 1961-2023: 10.68 bp/day excess return on announcement days (FOMC, payrolls, GDP, ISM, earlier of CPI/PPI; t 5.36) vs 0.93 bp otherwise; FOMC 17.61 bp, non-FOMC 8.65 bp (t 3.71); Jan 2020-Aug 2023 16.33 bp per announcement; FOMC premium low 2016-2019 (Kurov-Wolfe-Gilbert 2021). Reviews evidence that pre-announcement uncertainty (Hu-Pan-Wang-Zhu 2022), option-implied volatility (Jacobs-Ke-Pan 2022; Liu-Tang-Zhou 2022 R2 7.51%) and realized variance (Gafka-Savor-Wilson 2021) predict announcement returns; counter-evidence Zhang-Zhao 2022 (premium low when information uncertainty is high).
quote: At the daily level, the average stock market excess return is 10.68 basis points (bps) on announcement days and 0.93 bps on days without major macroeconomic announcements.
limitations: Working paper, index-level returns net of no trading costs; premium in 2021-2026 is unknown and the 2016-2019 FOMC premium was low; evidence that premium scales with uncertainty is mixed (Zhang-Zhao 2022 find the opposite for information uncertainty).
independent_replication: The announcement premium is replicated across papers (Savor-Wilson 2013, Lucca-Moench 2015 for FOMC); its scaling with uncertainty has several supporting studies but no consensus.
impact_on_spec: Gives the prior that announcement days carry a premium (non-FOMC 8.65 bp, t 3.71) that was larger in 2020-2023 and reviews predictors of it (pre-announcement uncertainty, option-implied and realized variance). The iteration tests whether a prediction-market uncertainty measure scales it.

claim: MIT-licensed fork of the FEDS replication package: Kalshi series KXFED, KXCPIYOY, KXCPICOREYOY, KXCPI, KXACPI, KXU3, KXGDP, KXGDPYEAR, KXPAYROLLS; public candlesticks; middle-out no-arbitrage cleaning of threshold CDFs.
quote: The upstream code is distributed under the MIT License.
limitations: Fork maintained by one person; an R pipeline with a daily, not hourly, grid and a trade-level path; consensus data are not in the repository. Our code reimplements the cleaning in Python and is tested on synthetic candles only.
independent_replication: Fork of the Diercks-Katz-Wright replication package; the README documents the cleaning but no independent validation was found.
impact_on_spec: Source of the middle-out monotone cleaning and of the series and threshold conventions; code is ported (credited in the docstring) rather than rebuilt.

claim: High-frequency election-probability shocks move energy, defense and clean-energy stocks contemporaneously; no measurable lag (evidence against odds-to-equity lead-lag).
quote: These shocks have immediate effects on asset prices in sectors that are differentially impacted by the policy platforms of the two major U.S. political parties.
limitations: Single working paper, election shocks only, sector indices; says nothing about scheduled macro releases.
impact_on_spec: Evidence that equities react to prediction-market probability shocks contemporaneously, so a lead-lag use of odds is not supported; this iteration therefore tests a risk-compensation mechanism instead and keeps the lead-lag row evidence_too_weak.

claim: Complete on-chain trade archive of Polymarket's first-generation CTF Exchange, 2022-11-21..2026-04-28, 1.20B trade records, 1.30M markets, with ground-truth aggressor direction; candidate data source for later Polymarket steps (licence and hosting to be checked at use).
quote: The dataset comprises 1.20 billion trade records across 1.30 million markets with $61 billion in nominal volume.
limitations: Abstract level only; licence, hosting and download size were not checked here and must be checked before use; ends 2026-04-28.
independent_replication: No independent replication; a data descriptor.
impact_on_spec: Candidate archive for later Polymarket history work; not used in this iteration, which relies on Kalshi candlesticks and a forward collector for Polymarket.

claim: Polymarket-focused dataset suite from October 2020: more than 3.29M market records, over 1.90B order execution records, nearly 21M oracle events; the paper demonstrates CPI expectation reconstruction for economists.
limitations: Abstract only; access terms and point-in-time properties not checked; Polymarket is an offshore venue with thin macro markets.
independent_replication: No independent replication; a data descriptor.
impact_on_spec: Second possible Polymarket history source and evidence that CPI expectations can be reconstructed from Polymarket prices; informs a later step, not this one.

claim: Information Leakage Score framework on a 911,237-market Polymarket corpus; the publicly documented insider cases are systematically deadline-resolved (0 of 24 FFIC inventory markets satisfy the original scope conditions); the abstract links them to no traded financial asset.
quote: 0 of 24 FFIC inventory markets satisfied original scope conditions
limitations: Pilot evaluation of a leakage-score method; the abstract links the cases to no traded asset and says nothing about macro-release markets.
independent_replication: No independent replication; companion paper cited but not read.
impact_on_spec: Shows the documented informed-trading cases on Polymarket are deadline-resolved markets with no tie to traded financial assets, so they give no basis for an odds-to-equity signal; keeps that use out of scope.

claim: Probed 2026-10-02 from this box without a key: series KXCPI returns 67 events (oldest listed CPI-21JUN), KXFED 52 (FED-21JUL), KXPAYROLLS 45 (PROLLS-23MAR), KXU3 65; KXPCE does not exist while KXPCECORE does (28 events); CPI markets close 08:25 ET on release day; historical cutoff for settled markets 2026-08-03.
limitations: A live probe written to a file by us, not a vendor document; counts change as new events are listed; KXPCE does not exist (404) while KXPCECORE (core PCE, 28 events) does, so the frozen PCE series is empty.
independent_replication: Event counts and historical routing agree with the macro_kalshi README conventions.
impact_on_spec: Confirms the series, the event counts, the historical/live split date and the 08:25 ET close of data-release markets that the data build relies on.
